Article Title: 'Not interested right now': Rahul Gandhi on Sonia Gandhi memoir row, cites 'crime' against Kharge
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Saturday said he had “no interest” in the controversy surrounding the upcoming memoir of his mother and former Congress president Sonia Gandhi, saying his sole focus at present was the “crime” committed against party chief Mallikarjun Kharge.The Lok Sabha leader of opposition was responding to a reporter’s question at his press conference on the “purification” ritual conducted after Kharge’s rally in Haldwani, Uttarakhand, earlier this month."I call it a digression strategy. I have absolutely no interest in that right now. My interest lies in the crime that has been committed against Kharge ji," Rahul Gandhi said, demanding "justice" for the veteran politican.The controversy surrounding Sonia Gandhi’s biography, titled "Belonging: A Journey Of Love," arose from reports that publisher Penguin Random House India had declined to publish the book after she rejected proposed editorial changes.However, Penguin Random House India clarified in a statement on Friday that it was not the publisher of "Belonging" in India.“Any suggestion that Penguin Random House India decided not to publish ‘Belonging’ because the author declined editorial changes does not accurately reflect the circumstances,” the publisher said in a statement.However, it acknowledged that it remained “keen to publish the book”, while stressing that fact-checking and recommending editorial changes were part of its responsibility as a publisher.“As a publisher, it is both our prerogative and our responsibility to fact check and provide authors with recommendations that are in the best interests of their books. This is a normal part of the publishing process. Throughout the relevant discussions, Penguin Random House India’s position was that we remained willing and keen to publish the book.We will not comment further on confidential discussions with the author,” the statement added.On August 20, the birth anniversary of his father and former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi, Rahul Gandhi expressed his excitement over Sonia Gandhi’s biography.“I am happy, and so proud, that your story—‘Belonging: A Journey of Love’—will finally be read by the millions of people who love you. I know how hard it was for someone as private as you to tell the world your beautiful story. Today, on his birthday, I can see Papa smiling and looking down proudly at his beautiful Sonia,” the Congress MP wrote on X.The book is scheduled to be published on November 10.
Article Summary: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi says he has "no interest" in controversy surrounding Sonia Gandhi's memoir. He says his sole focus at present is the "crime" committed against party chief Mallikarjun Kharge. The controversy arose from reports that publisher Penguin Random House India had declined to publish the book.

Article Title: ‘Jhooth ki goonj’ site ‘fact-checks’ Rahul’s student meet claims
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: With Rahul Gandhi looking to ride on the impact of his ‘Chhatron ki goonj’ initiative in his campaign against govt, a website, ‘jhooth ki goonj’, claiming to fact-check his assertions at the four editions of the event so far, has been grabbing attention in saffron circles.The digital counterpunch against Rahul’s campaign obviously complements BJP ’s efforts, but the party has denied any association with the website. The website itself makes no direct mention of the people behind it, but as it trended on social media, some attributed its creation to “nationalist researchers” and Gen Z-ers, the very generation Rahul is targeting in his hops across cities.“Here are all the lies Rahul Gandhi told during his so-called Chhatron Ki Goonj,” the site reads, making no secret of where it stands in his pitch against BJP. It says Rahul has made 40 claims in his four interactions, and all of them were either false or misleading (29 false and 11 misleading).It adds that Rahul had said that out of 1,000 youths looking for jobs, about 36 will get permanent jobs. Roughly, 300 will remain unemployed and about 700 will become gig workers, he said. Rejecting the claim as false, the website cites PLFS unit-level data to claim that 26 out of every 100 graduates aged 15-29 in 2025 have salaried jobs.Taking on another claim that Rahul had made — about 29% women faced physical violence — the website says he relied on old NFHS data. “Since the Modi govt came to office, the NFHS data shows a clear decline in spousal physical and/or sexual violence: from 37.2% in (2005-06) to 22.3% in (2023-24),” it says.How much impact the website will make is anyone’s guess, but it has certainly got pro-BJP voices on social media excited. “From tweaked numbers to fabricated stats, every single claim has now been fact-checked,” one user said.

NEW DELHI: A training aircraft belonging to Kanpur’s Garg Aviation crashed on Thursday, killing two — an instructor and a trainee pilot — on board. The Directorate General of Civil Aviation said in a statement the Tecnam P2006T twin-engine aircraft (VT-NBV) crashed about five nautical miles from Kanpur Civil Airport, near Ganga Barrage.“The aircraft was on a training flight in the local flying area of Kanpur Civil Airport. There were two persons on board, a trainee pilot and an instructor. Both sustained fatal injuries in the accident. A team of three officials from the DGCA is proceeding to the site for necessary regulatory oversight and coordination,” said the DGCA statement.The Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) has been informed and “will undertake a detailed investigation into the accident in accordance with the applicable rules. The circumstances and cause of the accident will be determined through the investigation,” it added.Senior pilots call for a thorough investigation into the flying school operations.On June 26, 2026, a trainee pilot had got grievously injured while deboarding VT-NBV with the propeller running at Kanpur’s Chakeri Airport. Following this lapse, the DGCA had on June 28 said in a statement that it had “directed VT-NBV aircraft should not be utilised pending the probe.” Subsequently the aircraft started flying again till it crashed on Thursday.
Article Summary: The aircraft was on a training flight in the local flying area of Kanpur Civil Airport. The Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) has been informed and “will undertake a detailed investigation into the accident in accordance with the applicable rules”

Article Title: Second excavation phase at Kashmir Buddhist site starts today
Article Text:
Excavations for the second phase of the 2,000-year-old Buddhist site at Zehanpora in Baramulla to begin on Saturday

ZEHANPORA (BARAMULLA): Excavations will begin Saturday on the second phase of Zehanpora, a Buddhist site in north Kashmir’s Baramulla. J&K chief secretary Atal Dullo will inaugurate the project.The presence of a 2,000-year-old Buddhist civilisation at the site was discovered last year by Mohamad Ajmal Shah, a professor at University of Kashmir. It gained prominence after PM Narendra Modi mentioned it during his monthly radio programme Mann Ki Baat on Dec 28 last year.The Prime Minister recalled that people had noticed tall mounds in Zehanpora for years without knowing about their significance. What were first believed to be unusual rock formations were later found to resemble three Buddha stupas seen in photos in a French museum.According to Modi, the blurred photos, thousands of kilometres away, proved crucial as it showed three Buddhist stupas, helping archaeologists connect the dots and reconstruct Kashmir’s ancient past. The discovery reaffirms J&K’s rich cultural legacy.It all began in Oct 2023 when Shah was on a fellowship in France and came across the 100-odd old photos at Guimet Museum showing stupa domes in Baramulla. “I immediately realised I had visited the site.What struck me was the domes in the photos looked much larger than what we see now,” said Shah, attached to the varsity’s department of Central Asian Studies.Later, Shah requested J&K govt’s department of archaeology to fund the project and it agreed. Shah and his team started digging in Nov last year, initially discovering a hall identified as an apsidal (semi-circular) stupa.Shah and his team also found iron/copper artefacts, needles, decorated objects and other materials. “We identified wall alignments through drone images and excavated precisely at those points. There is a strong possibility that many structures and artefacts still lie preserved beneath the ground,” Shah said.Shah highlighted the possibility that the site was linked to the Fourth Buddhist Council (1st century CE). “Kashmir was a major centre of Buddhism in ancient times. It was here that Hinayana Buddhism evolved into Mahayana Buddhism, giving the religion a new philosophical and cultural form,” he said.Shah pointed out that the Chinese explorer Hiuen Tsang had mentioned Baramulla in his travel accounts. According to Shah, Tsang spent a night at Uskur, a Buddhist site near Baramulla town and visited several monasteries in the area. “This suggests Tsang must have visited the monastery at Zehanpora as well,” Shah said.
Article Summary: The presence of a 2,000-year-old Buddhist civilisation at the site was discovered last year by Mohamad Ajmal Shah, a professor at University of Kashmir. PM Narendra Modi mentioned it during his monthly radio programme Mann Ki Baat on Dec 28 last year.

NEW DELHI: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat visited the Iskcon temple in New York during his ongoing US tour, where he participated in a food distribution initiative for homeless people and spoke about the role of Krishna consciousness in overcoming conflicts and divisions.Bhagwat visited the temple at 26 Second Avenue, where the International Society for Krishna Consciousness (Iskcon) began in 1966.Speaking to news agency ANI, Gauranga Das, a Governing Body Commissioner of Iskcon, said the organisation now has 1,300 temples across 120 countries.“In 1966, Swami Prabhupada officially founded the International Society for Krishna Consciousness (Iskcon). We are standing at 26 2nd Avenue, the same place from where Iskcon began, and today we have 1300 temples across 120 countries,” he said.Gauranga Das said Swami Prabhupada was credited with taking Hindu Sanatana Dharma to different parts of the world.Bhagwat penned a message during his visit, describing the venue as an inspiration and praising its contribution to spreading Krishna consciousness.“An inspiring venue which brought really a matchless gift of Sri Krishna consciousness to the world. I am humbled and surcharged with the feeling of pure sattvic love towards he who resides in everybody and everything.Heartiest thanks to all who arranged this inspiring event for me,” his message said.Gauranga Das said Bhagwat also spoke about how people could work together for global peace and harmony.In a post on X, he said Bhagwat offered a garland to Srila Prabhupada and inaugurated the distribution of the 100,000th meal under the Zero Hunger New York initiative at the Bhakti Center.Addressing devotees at the temple, Bhagwat spoke about the importance of consciousness in bringing people together despite conflicts and differences.“In today's world, there are so many conflicts, so many dualities. The only thing that unites is consciousness. That consciousness is Krishna Consciousness - we are one and we have been having it through these dualities of this world with the strong understanding that though there are so many diversities, dualities, conflicts, really it is all Krishna,” Bhagwat said.Anuttama Dasa, minister of communications and governing body commissioner of Iskcon, also welcomed Bhagwat's visit.“Mohan Bhagwat visited us and we are very grateful that he was here. A couple of weeks ago, Hema Malini was here. Both of them visited and we talked about how we can work together to try to promote God Consciousness and Krishna Consciousness values around the world,” he told ANI.He said Iskcon was seeking to promote an understanding of shared values at a time when the world was facing conflicts and polarisation.Bhagwat's visit to the Iskcon temple comes ahead of his scheduled address to the Indian diaspora at Madison Square Garden on Saturday at the ‘Universal Oneness Celebration’, being organised as part of the RSS centenary-year programmes.The event is being organised by American Hindus for Engagement and Dialogue and is expected to bring together Hindu-American organisations and members of the Indian diaspora around themes including shared heritage, interfaith dialogue and unity.The RSS chief arrived in New York on Tuesday as part of a three-nation outreach tour covering the United States, Canada and the United Kingdom.
Article Summary: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat visited the Iskcon temple in New York during his ongoing US tour. Article Title: 'Free insulin for life': Amit Shah celebrates Rakshabandhan with girls diagnosed with diabetes
Article Text:
Home minister Amit Shah marked Raksha Bandhan by spending time with young girls battling Type 1 diabetes.

NEW DELHI: Home minister Amit Shah celebrated Raksha Bandhan in Ahmedabad on Friday with local girls diagnosed with Type 1 diabetes.Sharing photographs of the girls — who hail from Gandhinagar, his Lok Sabha constituency — tying rakhi on his wrist, Shah posted on X: “Children with Type 1 diabetes require life-long insulin injections, which puts a major financial strain on their families. Under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, our govt is providing such children free insulin for life.”“This visionary initiative, which many developed nations are still striving to implement, showcases the commitment of Modi govt to the principles of “service, compassion and security,” he added.The home minister wished the girls good health and a bright future. “For the Modi government, public service is not merely a responsibility but the guiding principle of compassionate governance. Only when the health of daughters is secure will the future of the family and society be secure. This initiative to provide free insulin to daughters on the auspicious occasion of Raksha Bandhan also symbolizes our commitment to the protection and health of daughters,” he said while speaking on the occasion.Shah’s rakshabandhan gesture has a personal angle as well. The home minister has, by his own admission, reversed his diabetes by making major lifestyle changes since 2020.Speaking at a World Liver Day event last year, he revealed that by taking requisite sleep, hydration and the right food and regular exercise, he had almost ended his dependence on allopathic medicines and insulin.Type 1 diabetes, however, cannot be reversed or cured. It is linked to genetic factors and attacks insulin-making beta cells in the pancreas. Usually diagnosed during childhood or adolescence, it makes those afflicted with it dependent for life on insulin therapy.The Modi govt had earlier this year decided to expand its Rashtriya Bal Swasthya Karyakram to put in place an integrated system for screening, diagnosis, treatment and long-term management of juvenile diabetes.
Article Summary: Home minister Amit Shah celebrated Raksha Bandhan in Ahmedabad on Friday with local girls diagnosed with Type 1 diabetes. Shah wished the girls good health and a bright future. The home minister has, by his own admission, reversed his diabetes by making major lifestyle changes since 2020.

NEW DELHI: BJP leader Amit Malviya on Friday took a dig at Congress leader Sonia Gandhi over Penguin Random House India’s decision to "fact-check her memoir", questioning whether the exercise was meant to verify the author’s memories or address what he described as “the blurred line between fact and fiction”.Malviya said it was “rather amusing” that the publisher felt the need to fact-check a memoir written by Sonia Gandhi herself."It is rather amusing that Penguin Random House India felt the need to fact-check Sonia Gandhi’s memoir, a book authored by Sonia Gandhi herself. The publisher says fact-checking is a normal part of the publishing process and that it remained “willing and keen” to publish the book. Fair enough," Malviya said in a post on X."But if a publisher has to fact-check a memoir written by its own author, perhaps the obvious question is: what exactly needed fact-checking - the author’s memories, or the blurred line between fact and fiction?" he added.The remarks came after Penguin Random House India clarified on Friday that it is not the publisher of Congress leader Sonia Gandhi’s memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love in India. The publishing house also rejected reports that it had decided against publishing the book because Sonia Gandhi declined to accept editorial changes.In a statement posted on X, the publishing house said it had remained “willing and keen to publish” the memoir and stressed that fact-checking and providing editorial recommendations are a routine part of the publishing process.The clarification comes weeks after US publisher Alfred A Knopf, an imprint of Penguin Random House, announced that Belonging would be released on November 10. However, the memoir’s publisher or distributor in India remains unclear.An e-commerce listing has shown an e-book edition of Belonging available for pre-order at Rs 2,615, with William Collins, an imprint of HarperCollins UK, listed as the publisher.According to Alfred A Knopf, the memoir by 79-year-old Sonia Gandhi will offer a personal account of her life, spanning her childhood in post-war Italy, her marriage into the Nehru-Gandhi family and the assassination of her husband, former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi.The book will also chronicle her entry into the “public world of politics” following Rajiv Gandhi’s assassination and her decision to decline the post of prime minister in 2004.
Article Summary: Penguin Random House India says it is not the publisher of Congress leader Sonia Gandhi’s memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love in India. The publisher says fact- checking is a normal part of the publishing process and that it remained “willing and keen” to publish the book.

Sriram Kartik sweeps 10 awards including the ‘Best Junior contestant’ across Carnatic vocal and mrudangam; prizes presented by eminent Vidwan Sikkil Gurucharan on 23 Aug 2026 in MumbaiA fifteen-year-old from Powai has won ten awards at the Music Competition 2026 conducted by Sri Shanmukhananda Bharatiya Sangeetha Vidyalaya and Natya Vidyalaya, competing in both Carnatic vocal and mrudangam.Sriram Kartik, a Class X IGCSE student at Podar International School, received the awards at the prize distribution ceremony held on Sunday (Aug 23, 2026) on the occasion of Shanmukhananda's Carnataka Sangeetha Pon Mazhai Thiruvizha, at the Sri Shanmukhananda Fine Arts and Sangeetha Sabha in Matunga. The prizes were presented by Shanmukha Sangeetha Shiromani Vidwan Shri Sikkil Gurucharan, the eminent Carnatic vocalist, who presided over the ceremony.Vidwan Sikkil C Gurucharan is a leading Indian Carnatic classical vocalist and youth ambassador for the art form. A singer born into a family of flautists, and grandson of Sikkil Kunjumani, the elder of the Sikkil Sisters, he trained under B Krishnamurthy and Vaigal S. Gnanaskandan, himself a disciple of Semmangudi Srinivasa Iyer and gave his first concert at The Music Academy, Chennai at the age of twelve. Recipient of the Kalaimamani award from the Tamil Nadu government in 2020, Sikkil C Gurucharan has been featured by India Today as one of the 35 Game Changers Under 35 in India.Sriram Kartik won 9 individual prizes — five first prizes, three seconds and one third. He was also awarded a cash prize for being the Best Junior contestant winning the maximum number of prizes in the 10-to-15 years age category.The competition, the Vidyalaya's 70th annual, was held on February 7 and 8 across Carnatic vocal, violin, veena, mrudangam, Hindustani vocal, sitar and tabla. It drew more than 300 participants from across India and overseas, contesting in three age groups: 10 to 15, 16 to 28, and 29 and above.Sriram's two mrudangam prizes came in the only two categories open to his age group — a first for tani avartanam in roopakam and misra chapu talams, and a second for adi talam with five jathi mohras, awarded under the TS Nandakumar's Percussive Arts Centre Endowment and the Guru TS Nandakumar Endowment respectively.His seven vocal prizes spanned first places in compositions of the Trinity, varnams, Purandaradasa kritis; the Silver Lamp Prize for keertanams and kritis; second places in Subramania Bharatiyar compositions and Tamizh compositions; and a third in GNB kritis.Every prize at Shanmukhananda is attached to an endowment instituted in the name of an artist, a patron or an institution. He won awards under the following endowments namely - GNB Endowment, the Kalki Memorial, the Dr S Pinakapani Endowment, the BVS Iyengar Memorial and the Lakshmi Gopalakrishna Memorial. The Best Junior award came under the Smt. Parvathy Subramaniam Endowment and S Ramakrishnan Memorial.Sriram began learning the mrudangam at the age of five, under Acharya Ratna Vidwan Mumbai Shri Shankaranarayanan at Powai Fine Arts. A decade on, he has kept at it through the school years in which most students of classical music quietly stop — the age at which coaching classes, board examinations and the ordinary pull of everything else tend to close the practice room door for good.Sustaining it alongside school is the part a prize list does not show. Practice sessions run two and a half to three hours. Nine vocal categories at 5-6 compositions a piece meant something close to 45-50 pieces in which he participated of which he won prizes across seven categories, readied to a standard that would survive a judging panel, with two percussion categories besides.He now receives higher tutelage in mrudangam from Padma Vibhushan and Sangeet Natak Academi Awardee Vidwan Dr Umayalpuram K Sivaraman, and trains in Carnatic vocal music under Acharya Ratnakara Vidwan Sherthalai Dr KN Renganatha Sharma and Vidushi Dr Mohana Sharma. He holds a CCRT Scholarship for Mrudangam from the ministry of culture, and presented his mrudangam arangetram in June last year, the day after his fourteenth birthday.
Article Summary: Sriram Kartik, a Class X IGCSE student at Podar International School, received the awards at the prize distribution ceremony held on Sunday (Aug 23, 2026) The competition, the Vidyalaya's 70th annual, was held on February 7 and 8 across Carnatic vocal, violin, veena, mrudangam, Hindustani vocal, sitar and tabla.

Article Title: Delhi model murder: Accused Imran was booked under POCSO Act in 2018 for sexually harassing minor
Article Text:
Muskan Sharma was murdered, allegedly by Mohammad Imran, alias Aqib, at her home Wednesday.

Prior record

Suspect changed locations frequently





NEW DELHI: A city gym trainer accused of murdering a 21-year-old woman in west Delhi’s Tilak Nagar was injured in both legs during a police encounter in Rajouri Garden Thursday night. He opened fire at the personnel.Muskan Sharma was murdered, allegedly by Mohammad Imran, alias Aqib, at her home Wednesday.Police said Imran resisted arrest and fired at the team, following which the personnel retaliated. Three of the seven rounds fired by the police hit him in the legs. He was rushed to hospital, where he is currently undergoing treatment.Also read: 'Imran’s drug dependence, suicide bid, hotel meeting': More skeletons tumble out in Delhi model Muskan’s murder Police are also probing whether Imran had gone live on social media shortly before the murder and threatened Muskan that he will kill her. Sources said she had stopped taking his calls and blocked him on social media, following which he allegedly contacted her using different numbers. Investigators suspect he may have called her on the day of the murder and became enraged when she did not respond.Police inquiry revealed that Imran was booked under Pocso Act in 2018 for allegedly sexually harassing a minor in Tilak Nagar. The case also invoked sections related to voluntarily causing hurt, stalking, outraging modesty and common intention.Sources said it was not his first criminal case. In 2021, he was also involved in a culpable homicide case in which he allegedly assaulted a man who suffered serious head injuries and went into a coma.The complainant told police that on the night of Oct 30, 2020, Imran struck him on the head with a stone slab. While he was lying on the ground, Imran allegedly struck him on the nose with the same stone slab. He remained admitted to the hospital for six days. A case was registered next year, on court’s order.According to police, after killing Muskan, Imran allegedly took her iPhone, possibly to delete text messages and chats and prevent any digital trail from being recovered. Police said after fleeing the crime scene, Imran kept changing his location. Multiple police teams conducted raids across west Delhi and adjoining areas to trace him.DCP (West) Hareshwar Swami said Thursday evening, a police team spotted a suspicious individual near the sub-registrar’s office in Rajouri Garden.On closer inspection, the personnel identified him as Imran and tried to nab him. However, he allegedly opened fire at the team, prompting them to retaliate. Imran sustained gunshot injuries to both legs in the exchange. Eleven rounds were fired during the encounter; Imran fired four rounds while the cops fired seven, three of which hit him on his knees.As Imran remains hospitalised, investigators have not yet been able to question him about the source of the weapon and the motive behind the murder.Muskan’s family had told police she had been repeatedly harassed by Imran for a long time. Police said they also found that Imran suspected she was talking to another man, which he did not like.Police are also looking into the suspect’s Instagram account. His profile features posts about his gym workouts and cricket activities. However, a video uploaded from his account in 2019 shows a group of men sitting inside a room while music plays in the background. In the video, one of the men, who is smoking, pulls out a pistol and fires three rounds into the air.

A little over a week after landing Julian Reese as a throw-in from Washington in the Peyton Watson sign-and-trade, Denver formally waived the 6-foot-9 forward/center on Friday, according to NBA .com's transaction log. The corner of the deal barely got the ink dry before it unwound.Reese arrived in the deal because he fit a specific structural gap: Denver sits above the league's second tax apron, and two-way contracts don't count against the cap. That made him cheap enough to absorb even for a team with no roster spot to spare. It also meant his stay was never guaranteed. For Reese, who is the brother of WNBA star Angel Reese and spent last season fighting for NBA minutes on a two-way deal in Washington, the waiver is one more stop in a path that has run through an undrafted draft class, a Summer League tryout and three organizations in under a year.Denver's decision became official Friday when the team waived Reese, confirmed through NBA.com's transaction log. The Nuggets sit above the NBA's second tax apron, a status that blocks most roster additions. Two-way contracts, though, don't count against the cap, which let Denver absorb Reese's deal on Aug. 20 as part of the broader package that sent Peyton Watson to Washington in a sign-and-trade. The structural fit, not Reese's on-court role, decided his one-week tenure in Denver.Before the trade, Reese had shown flashes in Washington. We had sent him to Gurgaon to work and build his future,” he said.In his complaint, Harish alleged that the work was being carried out at night in the middle of the road without proper directions or indicators. Police said they are examining this allegation.A police officer said that on receiving information from the hospital, a team reached the spot and found the JCB, bearing registration number HR-36-AN-7050, abandoned. The JCB has been seized.

Article Title: ‘Go and educate yourself’: Anaya Bangar hits back at Marizanne Kapp over cricket return
Article Text:
Anaya Bangar hits back at Marizanne Kapp

Anaya responds to Kapp criticism

‘Baby steps from here’

NEW DELHI: Anaya Bangar has responded to criticism from South Africa all-rounder Marizanne Kapp over her bid to return to competitive women’s cricket, urging those opposed to her participation to “educate themselves” on the subject. Kapp had strongly criticised Cricket Australia’s decision to offer Anaya a pathway back into competitive women’s cricket , calling it “absolutely ridiculous” and saying “this should not be allowed”.The comments came after Cricket Australia cleared Anaya, daughter of former India cricketer and coach Sanjay Bangar, for a pathway towards elite women’s cricket under its Inclusion of Transgender and Gender Diverse Players in Elite Cricket Policy.Anaya, who underwent gender-affirming surgery in March this year, is currently eligible to play community cricket in any state or territory of Australia. Her eligibility for elite cricket from March 2027 remains subject to the policy requirements.Anaya’s potential return has generated reactions on both sides, with the 25-year-old now responding directly to Kapp’s criticism.“I think people who want to raise their voice against it should actually educate themselves on this topic, and I've already provided the necessary information in terms of not having any unfair advantage, and also complying with the guidelines set by Cricket Australia.“If anyone's personal opinion is in that sort of way, I hope they go and educate themselves,” she said with a shrug while speaking to PTI.Anaya is hoping to eventually pursue a pathway to the Women’s Big Bash League, although she is yet to sign up with a local club. Her immediate focus is on playing at the community level and proving herself through her performances.Anaya said she had spent a long period in “survival mode” and was only now beginning to process everything she had experienced during her transition and the long road back to cricket.“...basically now, the next role is to go there and play club cricket and prove myself by my performances, and if I do well, I hopefully might have a chance to be picked for the Women's Big Bash League. So, baby steps from here, but the major part of having a place to play has been cleared,” she said.She is currently in talks with a few cricket clubs and is waiting to decide on the right one “to go there and start playing.”For Anaya, the CA decision represents a significant breakthrough after years away from competitive cricket. While she has been given a pathway, it does not guarantee selection in any team.Anaya further added that the process was neither “automatic or informal”, with CA considering her medical and surgical history, hormone and testosterone levels, cricketing background, playing footage and scientific and athletic performance work undertaken with Manchester Metropolitan University’s Institute of Sport.She also said her most recent blood test in July recorded total testosterone at 0.6 nanomoles, which she said was within the female reference range reported by the laboratory.
Article Summary: Anaya Bangar has responded to criticism from South Africa all-rounder Marizanne Kapp over her bid to return to competitive women’s cricket. Cricket Australia cleared Anaya, daughter of former India cricketer and coach Sanjay Bangar, for a pathway towards elite women's cricket under its Inclusion of Transgender and Gender Diverse Players in Elite Cricket Policy. Anaya underwent gender-affirming surgery in March.

Article Title: Javed Miandad's emotional Imran Khan plea: 'What will happen if you let him out?'

Pakistan batting great Javed Miandad broke down in tears while speaking about the imprisonment of his former teammate and captain Imran Khan, insisting that Khan is not corrupt and appealing for his release.Miandad, 69, played in six World Cups between 1975 and 1996 and was part of the Pakistan team that won the 1992 World Cup under Khan's captaincy.Khan, who served as Pakistan's Prime Minister from 2018 to 2022, has been in jail since 2023 after being convicted on corruption charges.Miandad's comments came after Khan underwent a medical examination in Islamabad before being taken back to Adiala Jail in Rawalpindi. Khan's party has questioned the way the examination was conducted, pointing out that Pakistan's Supreme Court had ordered his transfer to Shifa International Hospital, where he was to have access to a team of doctors, including his personal physician.The issue around Khan's health has also been raised by his sons. On Thursday, Sulaiman and Kasim Khan spoke to former England cricketer Michael Atherton at Lord's during the second Test between England and Pakistan.They said their father's condition was deteriorating and alleged that he was being kept in isolation for nearly 23 hours a day.Speaking about his former captain's continued imprisonment, Miandad became emotional as he defended Khan's character.“He is an honest man. He is not someone who engages in corrupt practices, otherwise he would have done a lot of things. What will happen if you let him out? Will he harm someone? He is also someone’s son. I always think about what he must be doing,” Miandad said on the Narrative YouTube channel.Miandad and Khan were among the players who helped Pakistan become a force in international cricket during the 1980s and 1990s.Their partnership was key to Pakistan's 1992 World Cup campaign. In the final against England at the Melbourne Cricket Ground, Pakistan were in trouble early in their innings before Khan and Miandad put together a 134-run partnership.Pakistan went on to win the match and claim their first World Cup title.The issue gained further attention on Thursday after reports said the Pakistan team had threatened not to take the field following an interview given by Khan's sons to a British broadcaster.Kasim Khan accused those holding his father of deliberately prolonging his imprisonment.“It’s very, very clear what they’re doing, which is they’re just blatantly trying to kill him in there,” Khan’s son, Kasim claimed. “They just want to keep him in there as long as possible and hopefully just silence him,” he added.

Article Title: After 75 years the Pro Bowl is dead: Here's what replaces the game nobody wanted to watch
Article Text:
NFL ends the Pro Bowl game after 75 years (Via X)

Why did the NFL cancel the Pro Bowl game?

What happens to the Pro Bowl now that the game is gone?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The NFL officially ended the Pro Bowl game on Wednesday, closing out a 75-year tradition that had slowly lost the plot. The league announced at its owners meeting in Atlanta that no game will be played after this season. Players selected as Pro Bowlers will still receive the honor and gather in Los Angeles for a celebration, but the actual football game is gone. This is not a pause. The NFL is not regrouping. It is a full stop on what had become the most skippable event on the sports calendar.The honest answer is that the players stopped caring, and the league finally admitted it out loud. NFL executive vice president of football operations Troy Vincent spoke directly with more than a dozen star players this summer, and what he heard was consistent. They did not want competitive football after the playoffs ended. Vincent put it plainly at the owners meeting: "You come off the championship games and the viewers see the physicality of the game and you try to replicate that. Frankly, it just doesn't sit well. This isn't a good representation."That admission matters more than it might seem. For years the NFL kept pushing the format, hoping a tweak would fix the problem.The game moved out of Honolulu, the home it had for decades. In 2023 the league switched entirely to flag football, hoping the casual format would generate energy. It did not. Ratings stayed soft. Players showed up out of obligation, not excitement. Nobody was fooled.Peter O'Reilly, the NFL's executive vice president overseeing events, framed the decision with uncommon directness. "It's OK to be the first league to walk away from a competitive all-star game," he said in Atlanta. That line will not make headlines for its poetry, but it signals something real: the NFL is no longer interested in defending a product it cannot fix.The title survives. The game does not. The NFL confirmed that 88 players will still earn Pro Bowl recognition after this season and be honored at an event in Los Angeles. Several flag football exhibitions will take place around that time, though they will serve as entertainment rather than competition. The core distinction, being named one of the best at your position in the NFL, stays intact.The league also eliminated replacement selections going forward. In the past, injured players or Super Bowl participants were swapped out for alternates, which diluted the honor. Cleveland Browns rookie quarterback Shedeur Sanders made the Pro Bowl this year as a replacement. Under the new structure, that category is gone. If a player earns it, they earn it outright.O'Reilly explained the thinking behind the restructured honor: "The Pro Bowl has always been about recognizing the players who distinguish themselves as the very best in the NFL. A Pro Bowl selection will return to its original purpose, honoring the best of the best. We want that distinction to carry even greater meaning for the players, their families, their clubs and our fans."The voting process stays the same: an equal split between players, coaches, and fans. What changes is the weight behind it. Without a game to water things down, a Pro Bowl selection becomes a cleaner acknowledgment of a great season rather than a footnote to an event most people forgot was happening.
Article Summary: The Pro Bowl game will not be played after this season, the NFL announced Wednesday. The league says the players did not want competitive football after the playoffs ended. The game moved out of Honolulu, the home it had for decades, and the league switched to flag football.

Article Title: Inspiring story of the day: “I almost died after giving birth to my daughter.” - How Serena Williams turned life-threatening motherhood and family strength into sporting resilience
Article Text:
Serena Williams makes Cincinnati return with Venus after ‘emotional’ family moment with daughters Olympia and Adira

How did Serena Williams almost die after giving birth to Alexis Olympia Ohanian Jr.

How did Alexis Ohanian support Serena Williams during her recovery

How did Alexis Olympia Ohanian Jr. become Serena Williams’ motivation

Why did Serena Williams choose family when she stepped away from tennis

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Serena Williams’ story of motherhood is also a story of survival. In 2017, the tennis star won the Australian Open while eight weeks pregnant, then nearly died after giving birth to her daughter, Alexis Olympia Ohanian Jr. An emergency C-section was followed by a pulmonary embolism, more surgery and six weeks in bed. Serena later returned to the highest level of tennis, reaching four straight Grand Slam finals. Her daughter Olympia became an important part of that journey. Years later, Serena chose to step away from singles tennis to focus on her family, while continuing to build her life beyond the court.Serena’s pregnancy had gone well, but the birth of Olympia on September 1, 2017, quickly became dangerous. Olympia was delivered by emergency C-section after her heart rate dropped sharply during contractions. The surgery itself went well, and Serena was able to hold her daughter. The serious problems started about a day later.Serena suddenly had trouble breathing. Because she had a history of blood clots, she suspected she was having another pulmonary embolism, a condition in which a blood clot blocks blood flow in the lungs.She asked for a CT scan and blood thinner treatment. Doctors later found several small clots in her lungs.The treatment then caused another problem. Serena’s intense coughing made her C-section wound open. Doctors found a large hematoma, or a collection of blood, in her abdomen. She needed more surgery and another procedure to help stop future clots from reaching her lungs. After leaving the hospital, Serena spent the first six weeks of motherhood in bed and had difficulty even walking.Serena later described the experience in a CNN opinion piece, making clear just how close she believed she had come to losing her life.“I almost died after giving birth to my daughter, Olympia. Yet I consider myself fortunate… When I finally made it home to my family, with only days left in my recovery, I felt a deep sense of gratitude just to hold my baby girl in my arms.”The CNN piece was also about the wider problem of maternal health and the need for better access to care. Serena credited the doctors and nurses who treated her with helping save her life.For Serena, recovering from childbirth was not only about getting her body strong enough to play tennis again. She was also learning how to care for a newborn while she was unable to move normally.Her husband, Alexis Ohanian, was there during that difficult period. In Serena’s 2018 Vogue interview, Ohanian spoke about how hard it was to watch his wife struggle while he could not take away what she was going through. Serena also described how difficult those first weeks were as a new mother.That made her return to tennis different from any comeback she had made before. She was not simply trying to get her ranking back. She was trying to find a way to be a professional athlete and a mother at the same time.When Serena returned to competition, she faced another challenge. After her long break, she had fallen far down the rankings and had to work her way back into major events. She eventually reached the 2018 Wimbledon final, less than a year after giving birth.Olympia was born into a world where her mother was already one of the biggest names in tennis. But after the difficult birth, motherhood gave Serena a different reason to keep going.During her return, Serena spoke openly about the emotional side of being a mother and an athlete. Her run to the Wimbledon final in 2018 became one of the clearest signs that she could still compete at the highest level after everything her body had gone through.After the Wimbledon final, Serena also dedicated her performance to mothers watching her. She had lost to Angelique Kerber, but the result did not take away from what she had achieved by reaching the final so soon after giving birth.“Olympia, does mama look good out here? You’re the reason I’m here, you’re my motivation. To all the moms out there, I was playing for you today. It’s okay to have hard days, but we keep fighting.”That message summed up what her comeback had come to mean. Serena was not hiding the difficult parts of motherhood. She was showing that returning to work after having a child can involve fear, setbacks and days when the body simply does not cooperate.Her run did not stop at Wimbledon. Serena reached four straight Grand Slam singles finals after becoming a mother: Wimbledon and the US Open in 2018, followed by the Australian Open and Wimbledon in 2019. She did not win those finals, but reaching them showed how quickly she had returned to the top of the sport.By 2022, Serena was ready for another major change. She did not want to call it retirement. In her Vogue essay announcing her decision to move away from professional tennis, she called it an “evolution.”Her decision was closely tied to her family. Serena wrote about Olympia’s wish to become a big sister and her own desire to have another child. At the same time, she wanted to give more attention to Serena Ventures and the other parts of her life that had grown alongside her tennis career.“I have never liked the word retirement… Maybe the best word to describe what I’m up to is evolution. I’m here to tell you that I’m evolving away from tennis, toward other things that are important to me… My daughter wants to be a big sister, and I want to be there for my family.”Vogue published Serena’s essay in August 2022, ahead of what she described as her final US Open. She later welcomed her second daughter, Adira River Ohanian, with Alexis Ohanian in August 2023.Serena’s tennis story has since taken another unexpected turn. In 2026, she returned to competitive tennis, making her comeback first in doubles and later joining Carlos Alcaraz for the US Open mixed doubles event. That means her relationship with the sport is still evolving, even after she stepped away from singles competition in 2022.Her motherhood journey remains one of the most personal parts of that story. Serena went from a frightening medical crisis after Olympia’s birth to competing in Grand Slam finals again. She then made a choice to put family at the centre of her next chapter. For Serena, strength was not only about winning another match. It was also about surviving, recovering and finding a new reason to keep moving forward.
Article Summary: Serena Williams almost died after giving birth to her daughter, Alexis Olympia Ohanian Jr. An emergency C-section was followed by a pulmonary embolism, more surgery and six weeks in bed. Serena later returned to the highest level of tennis, reaching four straight Grand Slam finals.

Article Title: "I’ve sacrificed a lot": Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders' director Kelli Finglass confronts the possibility of walking away from the America's Sweetheart
Article Text:
America’s Sweethearts

Kelli Finglass on Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders and social media criticism

Kelli Finglass reveals her future with the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

For Kelli Finglass , leading the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders has never been only about flawless routines and game-day glamour. Her role has placed her at the center of auditions, tough decisions, television scrutiny and the changing pressures faced by young performers. As Netflix’sreturns for season three, Finglass is reflecting on criticism, motherhood, vulnerability and the possibility of eventually stepping away.Kelli Finglass knows exactly what it takes to become a Dallas Cowboys Cheerleader because she once stood where the dancers now stand. She performed for the Cowboys from 1984 to 1989 before taking over as coach in 1991. Her career has since become closely tied to the evolution of the organization on television.The Netflix series has brought unprecedented attention to the cheerleaders, but that visibility has a downside. Social media criticism can follow the women beyond the dance studio, something Finglass says she has seen affect members of the team.She does not make a habit of reading online comments herself. Still, she understands the emotional weight they can carry.“The words of people, while they can be very, very uplifting...Like in my personal case with my skin cancer journey, the people that reached out to me were extremely supportive," she said in an interview with Vanity Fair."Words can hurt and they can also heal. I’m trusting humanity to help figure this one out because it’s a much bigger thing than I can solve. But the girls being busy and focused and supportive of each other is where our strength will remain.”That outlook reflects a major lesson Finglass has learned through years of television. The cheerleaders do not need to appear perfect all the time.Kelli Finglass has also reconsidered what leadership means as she has grown older. She says motherhood changed how she sees the young women she coaches and helped her understand the struggles they face away from performances.Her approach has shifted from demanding perfection toward encouraging honesty and resilience.“I spent practically my whole career trying to create flawless performances, and what we’ve learned through TV is that vulnerability is actually more attractive. People love when they can relate to somebody, and that’s been an unexpected “aha” for me—for these girls to not project perfection, but rather be honest about their victories and honest about their struggles, has, I hope, given viewers something to find hope in and find something they can relate to.”..Now entering her 35th season with the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders, retirement is no longer an impossible thought. Finglass says her family could ultimately influence that decision, especially as she looks toward becoming a grandmother someday.“I have, but we’re so busy, we don’t have time to think about anything except the next hour. It would be a personal decision. I’ve sacrificed a lot of time with my family. My daughter is married, my son is in a relationship, and when I ever get the honor to be a grandma…I want that time if and when I have grandchildren. That would definitely give me a heartfelt reason to go to a new chapter.”For now, Finglass remains focused on the next generation. Her story has become intertwined with the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders, but her lasting message may be simpler: perfection is impressive, while vulnerability can be powerful.
Article Summary: Kelli Finglass performed for the Cowboys from 1984 to 1989 before taking over as coach in 1991. She says motherhood changed how she sees the young women she coaches and helped her understand the struggles they face away from performances. Her approach has shifted from demanding perfection toward encouraging honesty and resilience.

Article Title: What happened to Alyshia Rushing? Mama A’s Alabama car crash death leaves four children, fans ‘heartbroken’

What happened to Alyshia Rushing? Mama A’s Alabama car crash death leaves four children, fans ‘heartbroken’

What happened to Alyshia Rushing in the Alabama car accident?

GoFundMe launched for Alyshia Rushing’s four children

TikTok creator Alyshia Rushing, known online as “Mama A,” died at 26 after a two-vehicle crash in Montgomery, Alabama, on Saturday, August 22. A GoFundMe fundraiser has since been launched to help the children and their father with their needs after her death. Rushing had built a large TikTok following by sharing videos about motherhood and everyday family life. Her sudden death has left many followers grieving.The crash happened around 2:15 a.m. Saturday in Montgomery, between Taylor Road and Chantilly Parkway. WSFA reported that police found Alyshia Rushing at the scene with life-threatening injuries. She was later pronounced dead.The crash involved two vehicles. The driver of the other vehicle, 20-year-old Landon Dunn, also died at the scene. An unidentified passenger who was traveling with Rushing was taken to a hospital for treatment. Police are investigating what caused the crash, and no cause has been released so far.Rushing was known to her TikTok followers as “Mama A.” Her account had more than 470,000 followers, with much of her content focused on life as a mother. Her four children were a major part of the content she shared online.Fans quickly began sharing messages after news of her death spread. One wrote, “One of my favorite TikTok content creators passed away and I just watched her videos a few days ago. RIP to Alyshia Rushing. Lord please protect her babies.”Another follower said, “Alyshia Rushing was my favorite content creators frfr. Watch her every night in bed! Seeing her videos now and knowing she’s gone and left behind 4 kids is truly heartbreaking! Like I’m really taken aback.”A third fan wrote, “RIP to Alyshia Rushing. So sad & unfortunate, she was really getting herself back together & flourishing. I really hope one day her children finds all her videos and sees how much she loved and cared for them.”A GoFundMe titled “In Loving Memory of Alyshia ‘Mama A’ Rushing” has been created for Karter, Raelynn, Zoey and Aydan. It also says the money will help the father “prepare for future expenses” so the children “can continue growing, learning, and healing in a safe and supportive environment.”The organizers also warned that other GoFundMe pages may appear and said this is “the only fundraiser authorized to support Alyshia’s children and their father.”Many followers are now looking back at TikTok star Alyshia Rushing’s videos as they mourn a creator they had followed through her family-focused content.

Article Title: Prasidh Krishna reveals his definition of aggression: 'It's about what I'm doing'
Article Text:
Prasidh Krishna (BCCI Photo)

‘Aggression can come out in different ways’

Krishna lauds Jaiswal

‘50% of the job is taking it’

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Bowling to the conditions

Poll Vote & Share your view What factor do you think contributes most to a bowler's success in Test matches? Bowling strategy and technique Fielding and catching Pitch conditions and analysis Mental toughness and aggression 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Every fast bowler has his own way of showing aggression. Some try to unsettle batters with eye contact, some stay calm, others rely on yorkers, constant appeals or words. India pacer Prasidh Krishna has a different approach - he believes his aggression is best shown through his bowling.Krishna credited disciplined bowling, strong fielding and an attacking mindset for India’s early success against Sri Lanka. The hosts were reduced to 8/2 before bad light ended Day Two of the second Test at the Sinhalese Sports Club Ground on Monday. India had declared on 503/9 after centuries from Devdutt Padikkal and Dhruv Jurel.The bowlers had only a short window to work with, but Krishna made it count, picking up a wicket with just his second delivery of the second over.Krishna said aggression is not necessarily about showing emotion or getting into a verbal battle with the opposition.“Yeah, I would like to say so. I mean, aggression can come out in different ways, and for me it is about what I'm doing when I'm bowling. It's very easy for people to get away or be distracted by what's happening in the pitch.There's too much happening, there's not too much happening, but I think the focus is still to come in and bowl those areas with full effort,” Krishna told the broadcasters before the start of Day 3’s play.Krishna bowled back of a length outside off and found enough movement from the surface to trouble Lahiru Udara. The Sri Lankan opener edged towards gully, where Yashasvi Jaiswal completed an excellent diving catch to dismiss him for one.Krishna said the wicket was a result of both the conditions and Jaiswal’s fielding effort.“Yeah, I think it was, there’s something in the pitch, of course. Maybe stopped a little bit. There was a bit of seam, and I think credit goes to Jaiswal for the catch that he took. It was an exceptional one. We have been putting in some effort on the field in practice, so I think it just paid off,” he mentioned.India had very little time to bowl before bad light stopped play. Manav Suthar then dismissed Prabath Jayasuriya for two with the final delivery of the day, leaving Sri Lanka at 8/2.Krishna stressed that creating chances is only half the job and the fielders also need to complete the opportunity.“100%. I think 50% of the job is bowling the ball there, getting an edge, but 50% is taking it as well, and we have been pretty good at doing that. I think it's also doing the simple things right, which we have been doing well, and that's what shows,” he added.Krishna also spoke about the need to adjust his length according to the pitch. He said the Indian coaching and analysis staff work together to decide the right approach for each surface.“Length is something that keeps changing with pitches that we play on. So we sit with analysts, coaches, and everything and decide on what's the kind of length that we want to be bowling on different surfaces. And yeah, natural length was something that I could say when I was not playing for the country, but when I'm here I need to be bowling every length that the team wants, and I'm trying to do that,” he concluded.
Article Summary: India pacer Prasidh Krishna believes aggression is best shown through his bowling. Krishna picked up a wicket with just his second delivery of the second over. India had declared on 503/9 after centuries from Devdutt Padikkal and Dhruv Jurel. Sri Lanka were reduced to 8/2 before bad light ended Day Two.

Article Title: Kangana Ranaut slams Kriti Sanon ad, asks ‘why would you tie rakhi in bikini?’
Article Text:
Kangana Ranaut stirred controversy by critiquing Kriti Sanon's outfit featured in a Raksha Bandhan advertisement

Kangana Ranaut instagram story





NEW DELHI: Actor and BJP MP Kangana Ranaut has weighed in on the online controversy surrounding Kriti Sanon’s latest Raksha Bandhan advertisement, questioning the actor’s choice of outfit and asking why someone would tie a rakhi while dressed in a bikini-style ensemble.Kriti’s jewellery advertisement, released ahead of Raksha Bandhan, features her in an Indo-Western outfit comprising a bralette-inspired blouse, cape and draped skirt.The look has drawn criticism online, with some users arguing that it was out of place in an advertisement centred on the traditional festival celebrating the bond between siblings.Joining the debate, Kangana shared a note on her Instagram Story on Monday evening, questioning the styling choices in the advertisement.“It's a wonderful time to be a woman. Our closets are full of variety of clothes, today's woman is a global woman. From cocktail dresses to lehenga cholis, jeans to saris, bikinis to salwar kameez, from all the options that are available to us today why would you tie your brother a rakhi in your bikini/undergarments? Where are all your styling options? Ha ha the advert looks intentionally creepy!” she wrote.The advertisement had already sparked a debate on social media, with several users criticising Kriti’s outfit and other elements of the campaign.One user on X questioned the absence of traditional elements associated with Raksha Bandhan, writing, “Where is Puja Ki thali? Why are you wearing bra in front of your brother? Is this a Raksha Bandhan? Where is Tilak?”Another criticised the outfit, writing, "Who dresses like this on rakhi ?"Kriti has not issued any statement on the criticism or Kangana’s remarks so far.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: Kangana Ranaut criticises Kriti Sanon's outfit in Raksha Bandhan advertisement. Actor asks why someone would tie a rakhi while dressed in a bikini-style ensemble. Kangana says it's a wonderful time to be a woman.

Article Title: 'Haven't achieved 1% of my success': Kangana Ranaut slams critics, targets Baba Ramdev over comments on women
Article Text:
Kangana Ranaut criticized film industry figures and Baba Ramdev for their remarks





NEW DELHI: BJP MP and actor Kangana Ranaut on Monday hit back at several film industry figures and yoga guru Baba Ramdev over their criticism of her recent remarks, accusing her detractors of targeting her for publicity.Speaking to reporters at Delhi Airport, Ranaut said she would not take advice from people who, according to her, had not achieved comparable professional success.“Every day, I see people like Ashutosh Rana — who says I bark like a dog — or the likes of Sonu Sood. Then there are people like Rakhi Sawant, who make all sorts of remarks about my character, and Taapsee Pannu, who insults my parents, my upbringing and my background,” she said.Ranaut described her critics as “failed” and “completely irrelevant” people who, she alleged, abuse her to gain media attention.“If you haven't achieved even one per cent of the success I have in life, I am not going to listen to you,” she said, adding that she would not tolerate what she called personal attacks.Ranaut also hit out at Baba Ramdev over his remarks on women, saying he had “crossed every boundary of decency”.“The kind of comments he has made about a woman have shamed society. Given the remarks he makes about women, I think he really needs to reflect on his perspective regarding them,” she said.The latest exchange follows the controversy over Ranaut's “Generation Gutter” remark while criticising protesters at Jantar Mantar. Her comments triggered criticism from several public figures, including Sonu Sood and Rakhi Sawant.The controversy also brought her longstanding differences with actors Taapsee Pannu and Ashutosh Rana into focus. Ramdev had separately criticised Ranaut's remarks about the younger generation, leading to a public exchange between the two.Ranaut, who represents Himachal Pradesh's Mandi Lok Sabha constituency, has frequently been involved in public disagreements with personalities from the film industry and other public figures.(With ANI inputs)
Article Summary: Kangana Ranaut says she will not take advice from people who have not achieved comparable professional success. She also hit out at Baba Ramdev over his remarks on women, saying he had “crossed every boundary of decency’ The latest exchange follows the controversy over her ‘Generation Gutter’ remark.

Article Title: Kylie Kelce gets emotional recalling the miscarriage that made her terrified to try again
Article Text:
Kylie Kelce

Kylie Kelce admits the fear of trying again after her miscarriage never really went away

Why she keeps returning to this story

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A fan question on Kylie Kelce's podcast turned into one of her most honest moments yet. Asked point-blank if she'd been scared to try for another baby after her 2018 miscarriage, the mom of four didn't hedge, she confirmed the fear was real, and it stuck around a lot longer than most people would expect.Kelce first went public with the loss last October, during Pregnancy and Infant Loss Awareness Month, explaining that a doctor's visit before the birth of her eldest daughter, Wyatt, confirmed there was no heartbeat.The timing made it worse, the diagnosis fell on her husband Jason's birthday, and she initially couldn't bring herself to break the news to him that day. This week's episode picked up the thread from a different angle: what actually happened once she and Jason decided to try again.According to Kelce, getting pregnant with Wyatt didn't erase the anxiety, it just reshaped it. In early pregnancy, she found herself checking survival odds on a near-weekly basis, and by the later stages of her second trimester, that worry shifted into wondering whether a baby born that day could make it. She's been candid that this obsessive tracking wasn't necessarily a healthy habit, just one that helped her get through it, and one that carried into her later pregnancies too.Kelce didn't have to revisit this topic; she's already raising four young daughters, and the loss happened years ago.But her reasoning for continuing to talk about it is straightforward. She views grief from pregnancy loss as something with no real end date, capable of resurfacing unexpectedly no matter how much time has passed or how many kids follow.It's a theme she's returned to more than once, and each time she's shared it, she's said the response from others tends to be more stories of loss rather than awkward silence.She was careful not to frame the fear as the end of the story, either. Her bottom line was that avoiding the risk entirely would have meant never having Wyatt at all, so for her, moving forward despite the fear was worth it. It's a message that fits her reputation for being unusually direct about hard topics, and one she's now delivered twice, in two different ways, likely for the benefit of anyone quietly sitting with the same fear.
Article Summary: Kylie Kelce first went public with the loss last October, during Pregnancy and Infant Loss Awareness Month. This week's episode picked up the thread from a different angle: what actually happened once she and Jason decided to try again. Getting pregnant with Wyatt didn't erase the anxiety, it just reshaped it.

The 2025-26 ABB FIA Formula E World Championship will end in London this weekend, with Rounds 16 and 17 taking place at Excel London on August 15 and 16. While the title battle is expected to be closely fought, sustainability will also be a major focus at the 2026 Hankook London E-Prix. The event is not only about the final two races of the Formula E season. Its sustainability efforts cover energy, waste, food packaging, community projects, education and opportunities for young people.As the championship reaches its season finale, the London E-Prix aims to show how electric racing can combine competition with efforts focused on sustainability and community impact.The London E-Prix will run on 100% certified renewable mains electricity, supported by solar power generated from Excel London’s eco-friendly extension. Track lighting and buffer zones will use dedicated battery storage systems. This will help eliminate the need for continuous generator use. Any remaining emissions will be fully offset.The event will follow a strict zero-waste-to-landfill policy. Non-hazardous waste will be sent for high-rate recycling. Surplus food waste will be composted on-site using commercial wormeries. Used cooking oil will be recycled into biofuel to power plant and machinery.Materials that cannot be recycled will be converted into clean energy.ID@undefinedCaption not available.Food concessions at the 2026 Hankook London E-Prix will use packaging from Notpla, a fellow B Corp-certified brand.The packaging is made from seaweed and natural plant extracts and is home-compostable. It will replace single-use plastics across catering operations and support a circular economy.Mobile provider giffgaff has joined Formula E as the championship's first-ever B Corp partner.The partnership will support the €25,000 Better Futures Fund initiative with Big Issue Recruit. The project will help 20 young Londoners facing employment barriers through one-on-one coaching, barrier-removal grants, refurbished smartphones with data and paid work placements during London E-Prix race week.Formula E and PIF have relaunched the Driving Force platform, which has already engaged more than 94,000 students globally.The platform uses gamified STEM learning based around the next-generation GEN4 car. It also includes trackside workshops during race week and aims to inspire young people to become future leaders in motorsport and sustainability.Formula E's Community Tour will give more than 380 local residents access to the event through two dedicated sessions.The programme brings together more than 15 community, diversity and youth organisations. It includes career-focused sessions for young adults and track tours for local charity beneficiaries, giving underrepresented groups behind-the-scenes access to electric racing.The FIA Girls on Track programme will return to London, with 150 young women aged 12 to 18 taking part.The programme will offer career panels, garage tours, simulator access and discussions on tackling online cyberbullying in sport. It is supported by Hankook, Motorsport UK and Greenpower.Each participant will also receive four race-day tickets, while eight selected participants will take part in the podium ceremony.Also read: 2026 London E-Prix schedule: Round 16 and 17 timings, how to watch Formula E Championship finale and more

Food concessions will use packaging made from seaweed and natural plant extracts. Mobile provider giffgaff has joined Formula E as the championship's first-ever B Corp partner.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Michael J. Fox: "I think the scariest person in the world is the person with…" - a lesson on humour, perspective and facing hard times with lightness
Article Text:
Quote of the day by Michael J. Fox (AP photo)

Quote of the day by Michael J. Fox

"I think the scariest person in the world is the person with no sense of humor"

Where this quote actually comes from

Why humour matters most during genuinely difficult stretches

How humour actually helps people manage stress

Why laughing at your own mistakes actually matters

Why humour can genuinely strengthen relationships

Michael J. Fox's own perspective on adversity

Why humour is not the same thing as avoiding a real problem

Why being naturally serious is not actually a flaw

Other memorable quotes by Michael J. Fox

"One's dignity may be assaulted, vandalized and cruelly mocked, but it can never be taken away unless it is surrendered."

"I am careful not to confuse excellence with perfection."

"Family is not an important thing. It's everything."

"Acceptance doesn't mean resignation; it means understanding that something is what it is and that there's got to be a way through it."

Why people still find meaning in this quote

Humour can genuinely change how a difficult moment actually feels. A stressful situation seems lighter once someone finds a reason to laugh, and a serious problem often becomes easier to approach once it can be seen from another angle. It can create a little distance from fear, frustration and uncertainty, even when the circumstances themselves have not changed. Michael J. Fox , the actor and Parkinson's disease advocate, put a striking twist on that idea. "I think the scariest person in the world is the person with no sense of humor," he said. Not being able to laugh, in his framing, is not simply a personality quirk. It genuinely limits how someone can respond to life, and coming from someone who has lived with a serious, lifelong illness for decades, the line carries a good deal more weight than a passing joke.This line comes from an interview Fox gave to journalist Amy Wallace, published on Reader's Digest's website. Fox is not really suggesting that a humourless person is dangerous in any literal sense. He is pointing at the seriousness that tends to surround someone who cannot laugh at themselves, cannot recognise irony, and cannot find any lightness in a genuinely difficult moment. Humour creates real distance from a problem.It lets someone acknowledge that something is hard without letting it completely take over.Life inevitably brings disappointment, uncertainty and real stress. Humour cannot solve every problem on its own, but it can genuinely change how someone responds to one. Being able to laugh during a hard period offers a small emotional break, and it can help people communicate when a direct, serious conversation feels too uncomfortable to actually have. None of this means every situation deserves to be treated as a joke. Humour and genuine seriousness can exist side by side.Stress tends to narrow someone's attention down entirely onto the immediate problem in front of them. A moment of real laughter can interrupt that cycle. Research into humour and stress has suggested that positive humour can genuinely influence mood and help people cope with stressful experiences, and laughter itself is linked to physiological changes, including a release of muscle tension. None of this should be overstated. Humour is never a substitute for professional help or a practical solution when someone faces a genuinely serious problem. As an everyday coping tool, though, it can offer a genuinely useful shift in perspective.One of the most valuable forms of humour is simply being able to laugh at your own missteps. Nobody gets everything right. People mispronounce words, misjudge situations and occasionally embarrass themselves, and someone who can acknowledge a mistake without being consumed by embarrassment tends to find it easier to actually learn from it. Self-directed humour also tends to make social interactions considerably more comfortable, since it signals that a person does not expect flawless perfection from either themselves or anyone else around them.Shared laughter helps people form real connections. Friends, colleagues and family members often use humour to build a sense of familiarity and trust, and a well-placed joke can break tension that a serious conversation might struggle to shift on its own. There is an important line here worth being clear about, between humour that actually brings people together and humour that humiliates someone else. Jokes built on cruelty or prejudice tend to damage relationships rather than genuinely strengthen them, and the most constructive kind of humour has never really needed anyone else to get hurt.Fox became one of the most recognisable actors of his generation through films and television, including Back to the Future and Family Ties. In 1991, at the age of 29, he was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease. He later made the diagnosis public and became a prominent advocate for Parkinson's research through the Michael J. Fox Foundation. His public approach to living with the condition has consistently included honesty, genuine optimism and humour, which gives his comments about laughter an extra dimension. His point was never that difficult experiences are inherently funny. It is that holding onto a sense of humour can help someone preserve real perspective while actually facing a genuine challenge. His decades-long relationship with humour, cultivated alongside a chronic illness he never chose, reveals that laughter was never a denial of hardship for Fox, but a deliberate, hard-won tool for maintaining perspective and genuine hope through real adversity.There is a meaningful difference between using humour to cope with something difficult and using it to avoid actually dealing with it at all. Some problems genuinely require serious attention and real action, and nobody can simply laugh away financial difficulty, illness or grief. What humour can offer instead is a small amount of emotional breathing space while someone continues addressing the actual underlying issue, which is really the whole distinction worth holding onto here.Fox's quote is deliberately provocative, and it should not be read as suggesting that serious people are inherently unpleasant. Some people naturally have quieter personalities, or simply express humour in a different way. The broader lesson is really about flexibility rather than personality type. Someone who can be genuinely serious when it matters, while still finding moments of humour elsewhere, tends to have more ways of responding to life's challenges than someone who treats every single situation with exactly the same level of weight.Humour is easy to underrate, since it can look insignificant next to more obviously serious qualities like intelligence or discipline. Even so, the ability to laugh genuinely shapes how people communicate, handle their own mistakes and respond to real difficulty. Fox's quote offers a deliberately provocative reminder that life does not always need to be approached with complete seriousness. There will be moments when humour is genuinely inappropriate, and problems that cannot be laughed away at all. In between those moments, though, holding onto a sense of humour tends to keep people connected, flexible and hopeful, which is really the whole point behind the line.
Article Summary: Actor and Parkinson's disease advocate Michael J. Fox gave the quote of the day. He said the scariest person in the world is the person with no sense of humor. Humour can genuinely change how a difficult moment actually feels. A stressful situation seems lighter once someone finds a reason to laugh.
